questions.text: I often yield to the group's preferred approach, even if mine differs.
I tend to measure a good day by how much progress I made on my own goals.
I tend to choose my battles based on what matters most to my own goals.
My body stays in a state of relaxed readiness regardless of the emotional temperature around me.
I often proactively define the criteria for who gets to participate in key discussions.
I tend to respond to emotional provocations with a measured internal response rather than a visceral one.
The suffering of people I see as outside my group rarely concerns me.
I rarely feel drawn to check in on people who are having a hard time.
A photograph from the past can plunge me back into the feelings of that era with startling force.
I can receive criticism without it sending a jolt through my system.
I clean as I go when cooking or working on a project to avoid a big mess at the end.
When I reason through a situation in which someone is suffering, easing their pain matters to me.
I'm comfortable leaving things unfinished, trusting I'll return to them when the time is right.
I feel that the weight of another person's struggle is something I carry with me, not something I observe from a distance.
I notice that my system takes much longer than others' to recalibrate after a disruptive event.
I would work a job I dislike if it meant my family or community benefited greatly.
I am wired to flag what seems broken and let the group decide how to address it.
I eat when I'm hungry and exercise when I feel like it, without a fixed schedule.
I jump into the deep end with new skills and piece together understanding through experience.
I maintain separate spaces or systems for different areas of my life to avoid confusion.
I detect when a friend group has a designated peacekeeper who steps in at predictable moments.
I find it easy to go along with the group's direction, even when I have reservations.
I feel most aligned with my values when I am serving a purpose bigger than myself.
When I'm excited about something, I feel it in every cell of my body.
Evidence that people are experiencing preventable pain makes me want that pain relieved.
I enjoy naming the problem and telling the group how we will solve it.
I tend to be unaware of when someone is matching my energy level to put me at ease.
I can feel when a social gathering has an invisible guest list that determines who was and was not expected.
I find that deflecting praise and redirecting it to others feels natural and right.
I routinely choose quality-of-life improvements for myself over gifts for others.
I tend to miss when a conversation has a dual purpose beyond its surface topic.
I do not naturally notice when a conversation between two people nearby is meant for me to overhear.
I am the type who creates the rules of engagement for a group.
I invest time in building habits that will pay dividends over months and years.
I feel like I have a sixth sense for when something is off in a social situation.
Evidence of preventable harm to others seldom makes me want to do anything about it.
